newsitem.title: UK: Wolseley up on outlook for U.S. operations.
newsitem.headline: Wolseley up on outlook for U.S. operations.

text.p: Shares in UK building materials group Wolseley Plc advanced to a nine week high after the company relayed to analysts a rosy forecast for its U.S. operations in 1997, dealers said.
By 1054 GMT, the shares were up 10p to 473-1/2p.

Concerns that the strength in sterling would cut deeply into profits pressured the shares last month, dealers said. Natwest was the latest brokerage to shave its profit estimates, reducing 1997 earnings by two percent, they said.
But dealers and analysts said Wolseley executives expressed optimism about the U.S. market.

ABN AMRO Hoare Govett analyst Donald Anderson met with Wolseley executives recently. Anderson, who has the shares among his top picks for 1997, said the Wolseley "seemed reasonably happy with the course of trade in their biggest market. There's no sign that the U.S. market will weaken in '97."
